text:
Logan Stankoven won a Stanley Cup with Carolina last season and has opened this one looking like more than a supporting piece. The Hockey Writers and Heavy.com are both writing about a breakout, and his last ten games explain why: 12 points, seven goals, against about 7.0 we'd expect at his ice time.

The best news is that it's earned. He's generated 5.5 expected goals on his own shots over those ten games (the quality of his chances), against 3.7 usual, and at 5v5 the Hurricanes get 63% of the expected goals with him on. The worry is the finishing: 11 goals in 18 games at 20% shooting, after 13% last season, and his line has scored 5.5 more goals than its chances. Evolving-Hockey also noted he plays with very strong teammates, which flatters on-ice numbers. Still, a second-round pick at 17 minutes a night getting to the net this often (91st percentile in home-plate chances in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking) is real. Our projection has him at 26 to 40 more goals. Even if the shooting cools, the chances should keep coming.
headline: Stankoven's breakout is mostly real
